cohort: 72 pregnant patients admitted with severe preeclampsia to an obstetrics and gynecology department at a tertiary healthcare centre in Jhalawar, Rajasthan, India over a one-year period.
finding: The study confirmed that severe preeclampsia is a significant cause of both maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, with 97.18% live births and 2.72% intrauterine deaths among the cohort.
mod_finding: 61.97% of patients with severe preeclampsia delivered by C-section, while 38.03% had a normal vaginal delivery.
gest_age: 72.23% of cases were >=37 weeks of pregnancy.
